assertions.name: red_replays_recording
assertions.detail: uses the recording's milk and date

final_message:
I added a failing test, `test_an_item_that_runs_out_today_is_in_what_runs_out_soon`, in `tests/test_api.py`. It reproduces the defect, and I haven't fixed it.

The test replays the HAR scenario against the API. It adds milk expiring 2026-10-21 and yogurt expiring 2026-10-23, then calls `GET /items/expiring?days=3&today=2026-10-21`. It expects `["milk", "yogurt"]`.

I ran the suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. The new test fails with `['yogurt']` instead of `['milk', 'yogurt']`. The other 11 tests pass.

The cause is in `Store.expiring` in `pantry/store.py`. The filter `today < i.expires_on <= last` uses a strict `<` on the lower bound, so an item expiring today is excluded. Changing it to `<=` should fix it. Items already past their date would still be left out, which matches the slice's "may ignore" note.
